newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Novus says boosts Carnarvon portfolio.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Novus says boosts Carnarvon portfolio.

text.p: Novus Petroleum Ltd said on Wednesday it has acquired seven additional licence areas in the Carnarvon Basin offshore Western Australia from WMC Ltd, despite missing out on WMC's interest in the East Spar field.
Novus said it paid A$6 million for WMC's interests in WA-215-P,TL/2, TP/7, WA-149-P and WA-263-P, all of which lie in the Carnarvon Basin, where it has existing operations.
The purchase would be funded from working capital and existing finance facilities.
Novus said WMC operated all of the licences, with the exception of parts of TP/7, and it intended in the immediate future to take on this role.

Novus had been selected as the preferred bidder for WMC's petroleum assets, including its 30 percent interest in WA-13-L, which contains the East Spar field. Novus had agreed to pay A$173 million for the East Spar stake.
Santos Ltd, however, said earlier on Wednesday it had exercised its preferential rights over WA-13-L, WA-214-P and WA-264-P, for a total purchase price of A$181 million.
"Naturally, we are disappointed that we have not acquired an interest in the East Spar field and the adjacent exploration acreage," said Novus managing director Bob Williams.
However, he said Novus had quadrupled its net acreage in the highly prospective Carnarvon Basin, and also acquired WMC's substantial library and data base for a number of the areas.
Block WA-263-P lies adjacent to the North West Shelf LNG gas fields, and a well was likely to be drilled in 1998, Novus technical director Phil Vingoe said in a statement.
Blocks WA-149-P and WA-215-P between Harriet and East Spar were prospective for medium sized gas, Vingoe said.
